newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to make foreign telecoms firms levy VAT.
newsitem.headline: EU to make foreign telecoms firms levy VAT.

text.p: The European Commission will go ahead on Wednesday with rules to force non-EU telecommunication firms to charge VAT on services offered in the 15-nation bloc.

The move follows a unanimous request by national governments anxious to defend their own telecoms operators from unfair competition and to preserve tax revenue at a time when every effort is required to meet tough budgetary criteria for the EU's single currency.
Under existing rules on Value Added Tax on telecoms services, companies based outside the Union do not have to levy VAT on their European clients.
But both the European industry and national capitals argue that the rules, adopted in 1977, no longer correspond to the reality of the telecoms market which has become increasingly global.

They are particularly concerned about the development of so-called "call-back" services, which allow companies and individials to dial a number, usually in the United States, and get called back with an open line to phone anywhere in the world without going through the local operator.
International calls made through such services or by using calling cards are usually much cheaper, partly because they avoid VAT.
On Wednesday the Commission will agree special rules valid for two years which will make European purchasers of such services, rather than the foreign service providers, liable for the tax.

This is until the 1977 legislation is properly revised, which should happen by 1999 at the latest, at which point non-EU telecoms firms would have to register for VAT in at least one EU country, Commission officials said.

European operators, such as British Telecommunications Plc, complained at a meeting with Commission taxation officials earlier this month that the provisional rules did not remove all the distortions to competition.
But the Commission's draft has remained unchanged, one Commission source said on Tuesday.
